A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LWM study. The main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support a complete comparison; appendix contents match after accounting for pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, language/chat and vision-language evaluations, ablations, training measurements and generated examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, ablations and qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: v3 emphasizes 'Blockwise RingAttention' throughout, but v1 already explicitly used RingAttention and BPT in Section 6. The architecture, progressive training, tokenization, packing, loss weighting and inference procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora and evaluated retrieval, language/chat, image/video understanding and generation tasks are unchanged. The appendices retain the same test examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Tables 3, 4, 8 and 9 and the qualitative comparisons. Gemini 1.5 is newly cited in related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Context lengths, model sizes, data mixtures, frame sampling, training budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3–4, the training-stage tables and Appendix F.

E4.justification: The chat/QA mixture analysis in Table 6, masked-packing ablation in Table 10, retrieval analyses and qualitative case studies are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains the three LWM 1M retrieval accuracies of 0.67, 0.84 and 0.69. Appendices A–E reproduce the same retrieval maps and examples.

T1.justification: No mathematical definition, assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised. The existing complexity and positional-scaling discussion is substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims concerning million-token multimodal modeling, packing and loss-weighting solutions, generated QA data and released 7B models are retained. Explicitly naming Blockwise Transformers clarifies an existing component without changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 replaces the anticipated benefit of more efficient shorter-video training from compact tokenization with an emphasis on processing more complex videos. Interpretations of retrieval degradation, chat trade-offs, alignment/OCR weaknesses and the other limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, timings, sharding, inference precision and code/model access information remain unchanged, including Appendix F. Repeated Blockwise Transformer references restate an already disclosed implementation component.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds discussion of sequence and hybrid parallelism, acknowledges Gemini 1.5, and adds citations to LightSeq and jointly trained autoregressive multimodal models. Five references are added within the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title and several passages adopt explicit Blockwise Transformer terminology. Related work receives a short expansion, and future-work, contact and acknowledgment wording is edited; the narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Page breaks, spacing and float placement change: Table 3 moves from page 8 to 9, Table 10 from 12 to 13, and Figures 9 and 11 also move. Figure/table contents and designs remain unchanged, with appendices identical apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves attribution and research context by consistently identifying the existing Blockwise Transformer component and discussing additional parallelization work and Gemini 1.5. The gain is limited: empirical evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged, and the 'largest to date' conclusion remains unqualified despite the new concurrent-work acknowledgment.
